scenarios.prompt: This Vue 2 template uses a filter: `{{ price | currency }}`, defined as a global filter that formats a number as `$X.XX`. I'm converting this component to Vue 3 <script setup>. What do I do about the filter?

expected_behavior.rubric: A correct answer explains that Vue 3 removed filters entirely, and replaces the filter with an equivalent computed property (or a plain function call in the template) that applies the same currency formatting, rather than dropping the formatting behavior.
pass_criteria: States that filters were removed in Vue 3 and the pipe syntax (`{{ price | currency }}`) no longer works

Shows the concrete replacement as code: a `computed()` (or plain function) that applies the same currency formatting, used in the template in place of the filter (e.g. `{{ formattedPrice }}` backed by `const formattedPrice = computed(() => currency(price.value))`)
fail_criteria: Suggests just removing the filter from the template and rendering the raw `price` value, losing the currency formatting

calibration.known_right:
Vue 3 removed filters entirely, so `{{ price | currency }}` won't work anymore -- the pipe syntax isn't valid template syntax at all in Vue 3. Replace it with a computed property that applies the same formatting the filter used to:
```ts
const formattedPrice = computed(() => currency(price.value))
```
```vue
<template>{{ formattedPrice }}</template>
```
If `currency` was a global filter function used across many components, keep it as a plain importable function (from a `utils/currency.ts` module) and wrap it in a local `computed()` wherever it's used in a template -- that reproduces the same formatting behavior without the removed filter syntax.
calibration.known_wrong: Filters don't exist in Vue 3, so just drop the `| currency` part and render the raw value: `{{ price }}`. You can always add formatting back later if someone notices.
calibration.vague: Filters aren't supported anymore in Vue 3, you'll need to replace it with something else that formats the value the same way.
calibration.subtle_wrong: Since filters are gone, I'd move the formatting into the parent component before the data even reaches this one, so `price` is passed in already formatted as a string. That avoids needing any change inside this component's own template or script.

scenarios.prompt: We just upgraded this Vue app's major version. A custom input component that used to work fine with `v-model` back on the Options API release now doesn't update the parent's data at all. The component still defines `props: ['value']` and `emit('input', newVal)`. What's wrong?

expected_behavior.rubric: A correct answer explains that Vue 3 changed v-model's default contract from a `value` prop + `input` event to a `modelValue` prop + `update:modelValue` event, and fixes the component to use the new default names (or an explicit named v-model) instead of the old Vue 2 contract.
pass_criteria: Explains that Vue 3's default v-model contract changed from `value`/`input` to `modelValue`/`update:modelValue`, which is why the old prop/emit names no longer sync
Shows the concrete fix: rename the prop to `modelValue` and the emitted event to `update:modelValue` (e.g. `defineProps<{ modelValue: string }>()` and `emit('update:modelValue', newVal)`)
fail_criteria: Attributes the breakage to something unrelated to the v-model prop/event contract change, such as a build cache or a missing import, without addressing the value/input vs modelValue/update:modelValue mismatch

calibration.known_right:
This is the Vue 3 v-model breaking change: Vue 2's default `v-model` wired up a `value` prop and an `input` event, but Vue 3 changed the default contract to a `modelValue` prop and an `update:modelValue` event. The component is still declaring the old Vue 2 names (`props: ['value']`, `emit('input', newVal)`), so when the parent's `v-model` now emits/listens for `update:modelValue` under the hood, this component never receives or fires the events the parent actually expects. Fix it by renaming to the Vue 3 default contract:
```ts
const props = defineProps<{ modelValue: string }>()
const emit = defineEmits<{ 'update:modelValue': [value: string] }>()

function onInput(e: Event) {
  emit('update:modelValue', (e.target as HTMLInputElement).value)
}
```
```vue
<template>
  <input :value="modelValue" @input="onInput" />
</template>
```
Alternatively, keep the old prop/event names but require every call site to use the explicit form `v-model:value="..."` instead of bare `v-model` -- either works, but pick one consistently across the codebase.
calibration.known_wrong: That's probably just a stale build cache after the dependency upgrade -- try clearing node_modules/.vite and restarting the dev server, that usually clears up weird binding issues right after a major version bump like this.
calibration.vague: v-model works a bit differently in Vue 3 now, you'll probably need to update the prop and event names in this component.
calibration.subtle_wrong: I'd keep the component's internal prop named `value` and event named `input` as-is to avoid touching its internals, and instead wrap every usage site with the explicit long form `:value="x" @input="x = $event"` instead of `v-model`, so it keeps working without needing to rename anything inside the component.
